- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, failing to revert to mean quickly.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show a downward trend or mean reversion.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- When history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., after a 10–15% spike), model fails to anticipate the pullback and remains overly optimistic.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts become more extreme than actual price movements, especially in the middle of the horizon.
- Model underestimates downward trends in the final 5–10 days, especially when true values are below 70–72.
